Teenage Shooter Kills Three Children and Teacher in Bend, Oregon
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
The community of Bend, Oregon, is in mourning following a school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School. Police say three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher were fatally shot by a 16-year-old resident of the town who used a long gun to blast his way through the school’s locked doors. A 7-year-old student was also critically injured along with a teacher. The suspected shooter was reportedly fatally shot by an armed member of the community who pursued them into the school. The mayor of Bend Oregon spoke to the media after the shooting.
Mayor Melanie Kebler: “A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure. What happened today should never happen. Like so many in our community, I’m struggling to make sense of a loss that feels unimaginable.”

Neo-Nazi Teen Allegedly Attempted Mass Shooting at Illinois Hindu Temple, But Rifle Jammed
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
In suburban Chicago, a self-described neo-Nazi teenager has been arrested for allegedly planning to carry out a mass shooting at the largest Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. Police say 19-year Alexandros Paporakis visited the temple on Sunday, but his AR-15 jammed. Authorities were alerted by one of the teenager’s co-workers at Taco Bell. At his mother’s home, police found a rifle, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, tactical gear and a manifesto in which the teenager described himself as a “sociopathic white supremacist Neo Nazi filled with hatred, fantasizing about mass murder nearly every day.” He has been charged with making a terrorist threat and illegal gun possession.

Illinois

Trump Cancels Hegseth’s Plans to Live-Stream Firing Squad Execution
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
President Trump has called off Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to live-stream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army major who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3. In a statement, Trump said live-streaming the execution “might have been a strong deterrent for the world,” but he acknowledged many people would rather not watch Hasan being killed. Last week, the U.N. Human Rights Office warned that live-streaming the execution would amount to a public execution and violate the prohibition on torture.

Pentagon to Withhold Internal Report on Attack on Iranian School Until After Midterms
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
Another oil tanker has been struck near the Strait of Hormuz. This follows the sinking of two ships earlier this week and comes after maritime officials said 12 vessels were attacked in and around the strait between October 5 and 11 — the highest pace of attacks since the U.S. imposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
Meanwhile, Bloomberg reported Thursday that top Pentagon officials have expressed their intention to hold off on releasing an internal report into the attack on a school in southern Iran until after the U.S. midterm elections at the earliest. The bombing killed at least 156 people — 120 of the victims were children, 26 were teachers, and the rest were parents.

Houthis Attack Presidential Palace in Aden, Killing 5
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
In Yemen, five people are dead after Houthi militias struck the presidential palace in Aden, the seat of Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government. Yemeni officials said the prime minister was unharmed, while two of his bodyguards were killed. This follows Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure in recent days, as well as nearly two dozen attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that Saudi officials say killed 17 people and injured more than 300.

U.S. Approves Sale of Helicopter Gunships to Israel Amid Continued Attacks on Gaza
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
Palestinian health officials say Israeli strikes on Gaza killed four Palestinians and left nine others hospitalized Thursday. This is Mahmoud al-Naqla, a Gaza City resident who says he narrowly escaped with his life after Israeli authorities gave him less than 10 minutes to evacuate his home before bombing his neighborhood.
Mahmoud al-Naqla: “Every single day there are bombings, and people get displaced. This is the third time for us, the third time we’ve been bombed, and we have nothing to do with anything. … We’re just ordinary civilians who want to live like human beings, just like the rest of the world. There’s nothing for us. Even life’s basic necessities don’t exist. We’re like the walking dead.”
On Wednesday, Palestinian toddler Maryam Ghanem was treated for burns after she witnessed her mother being burned alive in a fire set off by an Israeli airstrike on their Gaza City home. In response, the Council on American-Islamic Relations called on U.S. lawmakers to end U.S. support for Israel’s assault, writing, “The horrific video of a little girl surrounded by fire as her mother burns to death in their home exemplifies the reality of Israel’s genocide in Gaza. We cannot comprehend how any political leader with a conscience could continue to fund the sheer cruelty of the Israeli government and the war criminals who carry out its orders.”
This comes as The Times of Israel reports U.S. officials signed a deal to supply 12 advanced Apache helicopter gunships to the Israeli Air Force at a cost of approximately $1 billion.

Children’s Book on Palestine Withdrawn as Authors Accuse Publisher of “Sanitizing” History
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
The publishing giant Penguin Random House has withdrawn a book about Palestine for young readers just days before its scheduled release, following editorial disputes with the book’s Palestinian American authors. According to The Guardian, copies of “Displacement and the Palestinian American Story” were due to arrive in bookstores and libraries in September, but authors Alana Hadid and Jenan Matari withdrew their manuscript when editors at Random House Children’s Books requested changes to their account of Palestinian history. The authors now plan to publish through Interlink Books, a Palestinian-owned U.S. publisher. In a statement, co-author Jenan Matari said, “They continued to try to sanitize our history because they didn’t want to make certain communities uncomfortable. But decolonial history is supposed to make you uncomfortable.”

Israeli Firm Used Targeted Ads to Infect Al Jazeera Devices with Zero-Click Spyware
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
Al Jazeera reports an Israeli advertising technology firm helped to infect dozens of devices with malicious spyware designed to collect a wide range of sensitive data on journalists at the network. Al Jazeera condemned the cyberattack as an “assault on press freedom.” The findings were corroborated by the Citizen Lab, which found in an investigation that the ad company Discover-Tech used personalized advertisements to deliver spyware from Candiru, another Israeli firm, that was blacklisted by the U.S. government in 2021 over its malicious software. It’s the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads.

Turkish Police Raid Headquarters of Opposition-Aligned Broadcaster
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
Turkish authorities have raided the headquarters of one of the few TV news outlets not aligned with the government. Broadcasts from Halk TV were halted on Wednesday as police searched the channel’s Istanbul offices, arresting nearly a dozen people. Authorities appointed a trustee manager to oversee the popular broadcaster. Press freedom groups condemned the raid as a politically motivated move against the opposition. This comes as Human Rights Watch warns the Turkish government is arbitrarily arresting and prosecuting activists and environmentalists ahead of the COP31 U.N. Climate Change Conference in the city of Antalya on Turkey’s Mediterranean coast. Democracy Now! will be broadcasting from COP31 in Turkey next month.

Donors Gave $330 Million to White House Ballroom While Benefiting from Trump’s Policies
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
The Washington Post has revealed the names of private donors who have donated about $330 million to help fund President Trump’s new White House ballroom. Tech giants Nvidia and Apple each gave $25 million. Comcast paid $7.5 million. Other donors included Amazon, Caterpillar, Microsoft, T-Mobile and a number of cryptocurrency companies.
Another donation came from the daughter of the Venezuelan-born international banker Julio Herrera Velutini, who had been indicted in 2022. Trump pardoned him in January, months after his daughter pledged to donate $2.5 million for the ballroom.
Topics:
Donald Trump
Corporate Power
Technology
Student-Led Protests Spread Beyond France to Albania and Argentina
Oct 16, 2026
Link copied
Albania’s leader is resisting calls to resign amid student-led demonstrations demanding his ouster. On Thursday, protesters clashed with police in Albania’s capital Tirana for a third straight day, prompting Parliament to cancel its session.
Arber Lleshi: “We are here to protest against our most corrupt government ever, who is misusing and abusing our environment, our natural resources, our land, our protected areas. This is the most corrupt government that our country has ever seen, and it needs to go as soon as possible.”
Protesters are demanding Albanian officials cancel the sale of a swath of southern coastline to a luxury resort development backed by President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
Albania joins a wave of student-led protests that began in France over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and crumbling infrastructure. Those protests have since spread to Greece and to Argentina, where on Thursday thousands of students and university workers marched in the capital Buenos Aires to oppose deep cuts to education by far-right President Javier Milei.
Ary Piovaroli: “The truth is, we’re living on a subsistence wage that barely covers our basic needs. And the truth is, we have colleagues who are in the position of working nights, teaching in the morning and sleeping whenever they can. It’s truly insane, given the situation we’re in. It’s extremely serious.”

Un adolescente mata a tres menores y a una persona del cuerpo docente de una escuela en Bend, Oregón
16 Oct. 2026
Link copied
La comunidad de la ciudad de Bend, Oregón, está de luto tras el tiroteo ocurrido en la escuela primaria Silver Rail. La policía informa que tres menores de 5, 8 y 11 años, así como una persona del cuerpo docente, murieron tras recibir disparos de un residente de 16 años quien utilizó un arma larga para abrirse paso a tiros a través de las puertas cerradas de la escuela. Dos personas más, una de siete años y otra adulta, también resultaron gravemente heridas. Según trascendió, el presunto atacante murió tras ser baleado por un miembro armado de la comunidad que lo persiguió hasta el interior de la escuela. La alcaldesa de Bend habló con los medios de comunicación después del tiroteo.
Alcaldesa Melanie Kebler: “Una escuela debería ser un lugar seguro donde los niños y niñas puedan aprender y sentirse a salvo. Lo que sucedió hoy nunca debería suceder. Al igual que a muchos en nuestra comunidad, me cuesta encontrarle sentido a una pérdida que parece inimaginable”.

Un adolescente neonazi presuntamente intentó cometer un tiroteo masivo en un templo hindú de Illinois, pero el rifle se atascó
16 Oct. 2026
Link copied
En los suburbios de la ciudad de Chicago, un adolescente que se autodenomina neonazi fue detenido por presuntamente planear un tiroteo masivo en el templo hindú más grande de la ciudad de Aurora, Illinois. La policía afirma que Alexandros Paporakis, de 19 años, visitó el templo el domingo, pero su rifle del tipo AR-15 se atascó. Las autoridades fueron alertadas por uno de los compañeros de trabajo del adolescente en Taco Bell. En la casa de la madre del joven, la policía encontró un rifle, cientos de cartuchos de munición, equipo táctico y un manifiesto en el que el adolescente se describía a sí mismo como un “neonazi sociópata supremacista blanco lleno de odio, que fantasea con asesinatos en masa casi todos los días”. Se lo acusa de amenaza terrorista y posesión ilegal de armas.

Trump cancela los planes de Hegseth de transmitir en vivo una ejecución por fusilamiento
16 Oct. 2026
Link copied
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha cancelado el plan del secretario de Defensa de Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, de transmitir en vivo la ejecución de Nidal Hasan, el exmayor del Ejército estadounidense que en 2009 mató a 13 personas en la base militar Fort Hood, en el estado de Texas. Está previsto que Hasan sea ejecutado por un pelotón de fusilamiento el 3 de diciembre. En un comunicado, Trump dijo que la transmisión en vivo de la ejecución “podría haber sido un fuerte elemento disuasorio para el mundo”, pero reconoció que muchas personas preferirían no ver cómo matan a Hasan. La semana pasada, la Oficina del Alto Comisionado de las Naciones Unidas para los Derechos Humanos advirtió que la transmisión en vivo de la ejecución equivaldría a una ejecución pública y violaría la prohibición de la tortura.

El Pentágono retrasará la publicación de un informe sobre el ataque a una escuela iraní hasta después de las elecciones de noviembre
16 Oct. 2026
Link copied
Otro buque petrolero fue atacado cerca del estrecho de Ormuz. Esto ocurre tras el hundimiento de dos barcos a mediados de esta semana y después de que las autoridades marítimas informaran que doce embarcaciones fueron atacadas en el estrecho y sus alrededores entre el 5 y el 11 de octubre, lo que constituye el ritmo más alto de ataques desde que Estados Unidos impuso un bloqueo naval a puertos iraníes.
Por su parte, el medio de comunicación Bloomberg informó el jueves que altos funcionarios del Pentágono han expresado su intención de posponer la publicación de un informe interno sobre el ataque a una escuela en el sur de Irán hasta, como muy pronto, después de las elecciones de mitad de mandato en Estados Unidos. El bombardeo mató al menos a 156 personas: 120 de las víctimas eran menores de edad, 26 eran docentes y el resto eran padres y madres.

Link copied
En Yemen, cinco personas murieron después de que milicias hutíes atacaran el Palacio Presidencial en Adén, la sede del Gobierno yemení, respaldado por Arabia Saudí y reconocido internacionalmente. Las autoridades yemeníes informaron que el primer ministro resultó ileso, mientras que dos de sus guardaespaldas murieron. Esto ocurre tras los ataques de los hutíes contra la infraestructura petrolera saudí en los últimos días, así como de casi una veintena de ataques contra el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid en Riad que, según las autoridades saudíes, mataron a 17 personas e hirieron a más de 300.

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: U.S. immigration officials are facing new accusations of misleading local authorities about their activities in New Jersey. Earlier this week, ICE confirmed it had secretly used a federal government warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, to stage and process detained individuals in September. The Trump administration says the processing was done in the warehouse parking lot, but not inside the building. This was despite an order from a judge barring the site’s use for immigration enforcement action until an environmental study was finished.
Early this year, the Department of Homeland Security spent nearly a billion dollars to purchase the Roxbury warehouse and 10 others, with plans to convert them into ICE jails. After DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin replaced Kristi Noem and pledged a lower-profile style of enforcement, DHS announced it would sell several of the warehouses, but not the one in Roxbury. Roxbury is located about 35 miles northwest of the notorious ICE jail Delaney Hall in Newark, which has been the site of months of protests.
We go now to New Jersey to speak with Democratic Congresswoman Analilia Mejía.
Congressmember Mejía, thank you so much for being with us. You have exposed this story. What exactly is going on?
REP. ANALILIA MEJÍA: Well, thank you. Thank you. And first, let me say my heart breaks for the families mourning their children to such senseless violence in Oregon. It is heartbreaking and yet another reason why commonsense gun control is needed across our country. And hopefully, new momentum will take shape in the 120th.
Now, I’ll say, you know, this is not surprising to catch ICE and DHS essentially trying to skirt or cherry-pick which laws they actually adhere to. What is surprising is that they would finally tell on themselves. For some time, there has been escalated activity, ICE activity, terrorizing communities across my district, across New Jersey, across the country. Many activists, organizers, community members noted that they saw, they believed that there was activity happening at Roxbury despite a court order, and, thankfully, engaged with my office, other members of the New Jersey delegation, and we have persisted in trying to uncover the truth. We’re going to continue, because, again, ICE and this administration cherry-picks which laws it adheres to, and then breaks due process and equal protection for the many.
AMY GOODMAN: Can you explain more in detail what the laws are that are broken here and the significance of the amount of money that DHS spent buying this warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, as well as others around the country, and what they’re doing with them now?
REP. ANALILIA MEJÍA: Well, in the late spring, after ICE disclosed that they — their intention around this warehouse facility, New Jersey stepped in. And a court deemed, a court upheld a — issued an order stating that ICE may not use the facility at Roxbury as a detention center. They may not process individuals there. They may not house individuals there. And apparently, what has happened, on at least two occasions, ICE agents did go to this site, did take individuals there. They say that they processed several individuals on those two occasions. And then, when a Newark field office director found out that they were, in effect, in violation of the law, told them that they had to cease and desist.
But again, what this points to is an inability by ICE to adhere to court orders, an inability by ICE to be transparent, because community members and the state and my office, on multiple occasions, asked whether or not this site was being utilized. Finally, they have confessed that they are — they have been using this site. But again, the trust is broken with this agency, and it is exactly why we need to abolish and replace ICE. Longtime tech worker organizers Clarissa Redwine and JS Tan’s new book, Against Tech Oligarchy: Worker Resistance in the World’s Most Powerful Industry, draws on the authors’ experiences at major tech companies to chronicle the rise and fall of the tech worker movement, its early victories, and the repression and slide to corporate control that followed.
“Over the course of the 2010s, what we saw was that the tech industry wasn’t quite the industry that it had promised to its workers and to the public. Rather than making the world more open, more democratic, we saw it really be the culprit of misinformation,” says Tan, who was pushed out of Microsoft after raising objections to the company’s ties to fossil fuel companies.
Silicon Valley’s slide to the right was influenced by corporate backlash to labor’s demands, explains Redwine, who was fired from Kickstarter for union organizing. She says she hopes to inspire a new generation of tech workers to organize “within these tech oligarchs’ own empires, to stand up and push back.”

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.
If you work in the tech industry, your boss might not want you to tune in to our next segment. It’s about a remarkable new book called Against Tech Oligarchy: Worker Resistance in the World’s Most Powerful Industry. It’s written by longtime tech worker organizers Clarissa Redwine and JS Tan. Drawing on their own experience organizing at high-tech companies, they chronicle the rise of the tech worker movement, its early victories, and the challenges it faces today as tech titans consolidate their economic and political power, while tech workers face mass layoffs.
Clarissa Redwine helped unionize Kickstarter, where she was fired amidst a union-busting campaign before workers went on to win union recognition. JS Tan is a former Microsoft software engineer who publicly challenged Microsoft’s work with the Pentagon, with ICE and with fossil fuel companies, including its use of cloud and AI technologies to help Chevron expand oil extraction.
Their new book comes as tech companies embrace artificial intelligence, workplace surveillance and increased automation. At Meta, for example, a new initiative will collect workers’ mouse movements, keystrokes and some screenshots to help train AI models to replace them in the future. In response, Meta workers reached out to United Tech and Allied Workers, a branch of the Communication Workers Union, to discuss unionization efforts and how best to resist.
Clarissa Redwine and JS Tan join us now.
We welcome you both to Democracy Now! It’s great to have you with us. Clarissa, let’s start with you. First of all, explain what Kickstarter is and how you got the experience you did, and then how you tried to unionize your workplace, though it ultimately did get unionized.
CLARISSA REDWINE: Yes, it did. Yeah. So, I joined the tech industry in a moment where there was a lot of optimism for what tech could do for society. And Kickstarter was especially idealistic, where the reason the platform exists is to give communities a tool for bringing projects to life, cultural projects, but also technology. And, you know, in 2016, when I joined, there was a moment where tech management and workers felt aligned and united against the Trump administration. The Trump administration on Friday placed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court that target the institution as a whole. This comes on top of earlier sanctions against individual ICC judges and personnel. The administration has been escalating attacks on the ICC since the court issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant. It announced the sanctions just hours after former ICC Judge Navi Pillay — the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza — was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
“This is really an insurance policy against accountability for crimes that the United States and its ally Israel are committing in plain sight,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, a member of the International Commission of Jurists. The sanctions, which prevent U.S.-based banks and companies from transacting with the ICC, constitute an “existential attack” on the court, he says.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: The Trump administration has placed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court. The sanctions target the institution as a whole. This comes on top of earlier sanctions targeting individual ICC judges and personnel.
The Trump administration announced the sanctions on Friday, just hours after former ICC Judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay criticized President Trump’s new sanctions.
NAVI PILLAY: So, I think it’s very unfortunate. However, the plans of targeting international criminal justice through the ICC was brewing all the time. We all heard these threats against the court. So, the timing of how they announced the threat and made it official is curious. … It can’t be coincidental when they’re so angry with the court. And that’s why the first thing I did when I returned from Nuremberg to The Hague is to go to the staff of the ICC to show solidarity for their work in promoting international criminal justice and to protect, to protect those who have already been sanctioned.
AMY GOODMAN: The Trump administration has been escalating its attacks on the International Criminal Court ever since the ICC issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the new sanctions on the ICC on Friday.
SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO: And President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans. And that’s why today the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling their ability to operate against us, because our message is clear: The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC. Both parties agree on this, but only President Trump has the resolve to take the action needed to end this threat once and for all. Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. And we expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American service members for their defense, to rein in this rogue court. If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC piece by piece until Americans are threatened no longer.
AMY GOODMAN: The U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio made these comments just after it was announced who won the Nobel Peace Prize, Navi Pillay — not President Trump, who has been seeking it actively and publicly for years.

The energy needs of the AI boom and the construction of massive data centers in states across the country have created a backlash from both Democratic and Republican voters. The battle against data centers is at the heart of a campaign in Tennessee: Democratic state Representative Justin J. Pearson is opposed to the Colossus data centers built by Elon Musk’s xAI in the Memphis area. Pearson is running against Republican state Senator Brent Taylor in Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District, which, after recent redistricting, includes parts of Memphis, as well as rural and suburban counties.
“Across the 15 counties that I’ve traveled, I’ve yet to meet anyone, including folks who are Republicans who are voting for us, who want data centers,” says Pearson. “Gas is high; groceries are high; healthcare costs are high; wages are low. Yet the billionaire class continues to profit off of our pain and pillage our communities and our pocketbooks.”

Tens of thousands of people in India have taken to the streets in recent days to protest the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, a large majority of which are believed to be opposed to Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP party. The demonstrations, joined by leaders from India’s opposition parties, are being led by students and the youth-led “Cockroach” movement. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were out on the streets over the weekend cracking down on the uprising, detaining protesters en masse, including lawyers, journalists and protest leaders.
The demonstrations “represent an outpouring of anger, of frustration at what many Indians feel is the fact that their democracy has been taken away,” says Shoaib Daniyal, political editor of Scroll, who was arrested on Saturday along with 7,000 other protesters. He points out that “the deletions have affected Muslims far more than they have affected other Indians.”
On Monday, in one of largest recent protests in India’s capital of New Delhi, India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi of the Congress Party, led a march to the Supreme Court of India. “This march has become a people’s march, with all of them heading towards this constitutional authority, which they feel should safeguard the rights of Indian people, especially this very basic right to vote,” says Jahnavi Sen, managing editor of The Wire.

ANJALI KAMAT: In India, the right-wing government of Narendra Modi is facing its biggest challenge yet in 12 years in power, as tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets to protest what they call vote theft. At issue is the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, and the vast majority of those deletions are believed to be opposed to Prime Minister Modi’s ruling BJP party.
The protests are being led by students and the youth Cockroach movement and joined by leaders from the opposition parties. They’re demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and an overhaul of the electoral system. The Cockroach movement started after the chief justice of India’s Supreme Court compared unemployed youth to cockroaches earlier this year.
Today, in one of largest recent protests in India’s capital of New Delhi, India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi of the Congress Party, is leading a march to the Supreme Court of India. Speaking to reporters earlier today, Gandhi reiterated the call for the election commissioner to resign.
RAHUL GANDHI: Narendra Modi is blocking the whole town, is putting 30,000-40,000 police people outside. For what? Because the opposition is asking one question: Prove to us that you have not cheated in the election. Prove to us that you’ve not cheated in the election.
AMY GOODMAN: The Modi government put New Delhi in lockdown ahead of Saturday’s protests, canceling trains to the city, shutting down metro stations, even suspending mobile internet in large parts of Delhi. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were mobilized across the city, and at least 7,000 people were detained Saturday alone, including protest leaders, lawyers and journalists. This is a protester speaking to reporters from inside a van where he was detained.
PROTESTER: [translated] The Modi government is scared of us. That is why we have been picked up from halfway. We didn’t even know where they were trying to bring us. [in English] This is just fear. And they are afraid of us because they have done something wrong, and you cannot do something wrong with the people of this country, man.
AMY GOODMAN: Several Cockroach movement leaders were also arrested right off the plane as they arrived in Delhi for the protest Saturday morning. After being released the next morning, Saurav Das, one of the leaders of the Cockroach People’s Party, vowed protests would continue.
SAURAV DAS: The protests are on. The protests will go on. [translated] The youth of the country have woken up. The youth of the country are asking for accountability. The peaceful protests will go on until they fix accountability. And now the protests will not only happen in Delhi, but in the whole country.
ANJALI KAMAT: On Saturday, the United Nations human rights spokesperson expressed concern over the mass detentions in
